x: I am indebted to Jack Goswell, Alf Harley, Bob Taylor, Dave Sheppard, Bill Lucas, Charlie MacLennon, Alan Mead, Howard Satchell, to the general committee, and in particular to Chris Steer, Bernard Merry, Arthur Penstone and our indefatiguable barmen Frank Webb, Norman Dewberry and Tom Pritchard.

The club then honoured Win Shepherd, Tom Pritchard and Clive Shippen by electing them Vice-Presidents. The meeting really became alive when John Thresher raised the subject of sending a club cross country team to compete on the Continent.
Tom Pritchard, a member for over forty years, has been invited to fill the vacancy on Committee, as he headed the list of unsuccessful candidates at the Annual General Meeting last September.
KEN O'KELL first showed himself in 1923 and 1924* followed with that great walker FRED RICKARDS, TOM PRITCHARD and a very loyal member of earlier days, SYD KING.

The names of Ray Middleton and Tom Pritchard were then put up for Life Membership. Frank Jarvis spoke on behalf of Ray Middleton "not just as your Assistant Honorary Secretary, but also as Honorary Secretary of the Southern R.W.A." Ray had served his Club and country exceptionally well for many year…

TOM PRITCHARD, NORMAN DEWBERRY and FRANK WEBB who have given such fine sevice on those busy evenings have decided to join the horses from the Brewer's dray and enjoy some gentle running in quiet, green pastures away from that cacophony of sound at Belgrave Hall.

It is with great regret that we have to advise the death of Tom Pritchard who passed on at the age of 66 years. Tom joined the Club on the 10th June 1924, and I think he must have been the longest serving active member - 50 years.
